implementation: GPU public hashing exactly matches commitment::hash_fields: domain and length binding, four-word chunks, zero padding only at the end, and no permutations for an empty message
A fixed 4096-word input buffer and four-word chaining state keep all intermediate hashes on device; only the final 32-byte digest is read back
Registered GPU witnesses select GPU program identity hashing in the existing public setup session; canonical manifest, CPU reference hashing and independent verification remain unchanged
Preprocessing commits carry a DomainSpec directly, removing hidden CPU shift inversion during natural-domain construction
Worker witness reservations add 32800 managed bytes, a 32768-byte allocation bound, and 65536 host bytes, without reducing any existing reservation or changing caller metadata encoding
Per-batch device events and completed batch counts feed preprocessing/public-value stage reports; unsupported/failed GPU operations do not fall back to CPU

validation.proof_conformance: Full and compact registered GPU-witness and GPU-transcript proofs in wide release, eight-lane release and debug, plus registered GPU-randomness proofs in wide release. Registry identities and preprocessing caps match CPU; serialized proofs verify using original upstream CPU PCS/root challenger after GPU shutdown; altered public values reject. Owned transcript proofs retain exact single-thread CPU bytes.
validation.public_hash_conformance: Domains zero, registry tag and near-modulus; canonical boundary fields; empty/partial/exact-rate messages; lengths around 4096-word batches and through 65537 fields; a 131073-field message exceeds the 1 MiB managed test budget but hashes using fixed scratch. Exact CPU digests and byte/call/permutation counters match.
validation.failure_coverage: Late noncanonical input rejects before upload. Aggregate scratch and maximum-allocation shortfalls reject before allocation; injected failure after a GPU batch discards state and leaves a fresh hash usable. CPU-required policy rejects before work; actual batches/device times are reported without fabricated wall time.
validation.cpu_regression: CPU-only build, registered CPU proof, unchanged commitment/program/fingerprint sources, public-salt/preprocessing compatibility, and nine enabled policy/reporting cases pass. Production-strength CPU wallet proof remains explicitly ignored.

development_artifacts: The initial Rust build required an explicit usize annotation in the new boundary test. Its log is preserved at /tmp/lattica-gpu-setup-initial-type-error.log; final totals count only the successful build and run-01 matrix.
